Scheduled runs carry the cron context, so the order step needs no approval card. The three

the order fills -> open orders -> balance.

_note: The pipeline does nothing until the module settings say what to run and where. Two fields,
both human-only — the model has no tool that writes either of them.
`trades` is the wiring: which coin, which broker, which timeframe. The interval belongs
here rather than in the cron because the rule was measured on hourly bars, and trading it
on another timeframe would be trading something that was never measured.
`strategies` is the rule. It has to match the rules block above — this pipeline hands one
signal to the cycle, so a mismatch would mean sizing one rule from another rule's signal.
`lotSize` is the venue's smallest tradeable increment and it matters more than it looks:
quantities are floored to it, so leaving it at the default of 1 whole unit means a 6,000
won order on a four-million won coin comes out at zero. Upbit is eight decimal places.
Upbit also refuses an order under 5,000 won, which is why perOrderKrw is above it.
The parameters are the ones KRW-ETH cleared on 2026 hourly data, all fifty grid cells,
+18.9% out of sample. Start with mode=dryrun: no order is placed and the ledger still
fills, which is what makes the first week readable.
